messages:
maya: Running the 1k-concurrent replay run this morning and the numbers don’t line up with the synthetic harness. ~12-18% lower tokens/s on replay. Suspect kernel selection change after driver bump.

aj: ugh. which driver + image? can you paste the top lines (nvidia-smi, docker image tag, runtime commit)?

maya: sure — quick paste: 
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
Driver Version: 535.86
$ docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Image}}:{{.Config.Labels.commit}}' redwood/runtime:latest
redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-cuda11.8 (commit: ab12c3)
```
Kernel selector logs show a change around matmul pick for sequence len ~1024. Previously picked 'bmm_large' variant, new pick is 'mma_tf32_row'.

sasha: did the replay input distribution change? replay often has longer tails which can alter kernel heuristics.

maya: replay inputs unchanged — we use the exact same trace from last quarter. KV hit rate is identical (98.3%). The perf delta shows extra ~1.5ms per token during attention kernel stage.

leo: can you paste a small profiler snippet? nvtx ranges or perf counters?

maya: attaching snippet from our runtime flame (trimmed):
```
[ATTENTION_K] total 1200ms
 - tile_launch 400ms
 - matmul 700ms  <-- this ballooned
 - softmax 100ms
```

aj: interesting. if matmul is different, probably a cuBLAS/cuDNN or kernel selection path change in our fused attention. Which CUDA runtime/cuBLAS version is in that image?

maya: cuda runtime inside container: 11.8, cuBLAS 11.10 (from image label). But driver on host 535.86. Previously host driver was 525.60 and numbers matched synthetic.

sasha: drivers can change heuristics (tensor core path selection). We should reproduce on both host driver versions pinned while keeping the container constant. Also test across A100 vs H100 (we have both in the lab).

runtime-bot: created a perf matrix run: a100,h100 x driver(525.60,535.86) x image(redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-cuda11.8) — 2 seeds. job: #perf-9123

aj: maya — please run the replay harness with NVTX and upload trace.json for both driver pins. use: 
```
RUNTIME_TRACE=1 RUNTIME_NVTX=1 ./tools/replay_harness --trace --seed=42 --out=trace-driver525.json
```

and same on driver535 host.

maya: started driver525 run now on a100 (host with driver 525.60). will post traces.

(an hour later)

maya: results in. Quick summary:
 - driver525 @ A100: 18.2k tokens/s (replay)
 - driver535 @ A100: 15.1k tokens/s (replay)
 - synthetic harness (driver535 @ A100): 17.9k tokens/s
So synthetic was close to driver525 replay, but replay under driver535 regressed.

leo: that narrows it to driver change interacting with replay path. Do traces show additional memcpy or kernel launches?

maya: yes — trace shows an extra cudaMemcpyAsync to staging buffer before matmul for ~0.6ms per invocation. The synthetic harness does not trigger that copy because of alignment differences in batched sizes.

sasha: KV cache behavior might be altering tensor shapes (slice+concat) such that our kernel selection falls into a slower codepath. We should add a micro-benchmark: run the attention micro with the exact KV concat shapes from replay.

aj: also try setting our kernel-override env to force the old matmul variant to see if perf returns (quick guardrail):
```
RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_bmm_large ./tools/replay_harness --seed=42
```

maya: forced; tokens/s jumped to 18.0k on driver535. So it's clearly a kernel pick issue.

anita: nice repro. action items: 1) create deterministic microbench for attention shapes from replay (maya) 2) add guard flag to runtime to pin kernel for affected shape (aj) 3) coordinate with infra to decide whether to pin driver or push runtime fix (anita).

ci-bot: created ticket PERF-2384: "Driver 535 kernel-selection regression for replay attention shapes" and linked job #perf-9123.

leo: for long term, we should add our kernel selection stability tests to the CI perf matrix: compare kernel picks across driver and image combos, fail if heuristic flips for identical shapes without config change.

sasha: agree. also add a small opt-in test to synthetic harness that mimics replay alignment fuzz so synthetic isn't blind to these cases.

maya: I will upload NVTX trace + pprof stacks to the ticket and attach the microbench code. 

aj: one more datapoint — on H100 host with driver535 the regression is smaller (~6%) vs A100 where it was ~16%. suggests driver+arch interaction. include both GPUs in the perf matrix.

anita: assigned PERF-2384 to aj/maya. ETA for microbench + kernel-override PR: EOW. infra will run full matrix next week.

maya: thanks — will follow up with trace links and the microbench gist in the ticket. :thumbsup:
